archetypes.name: quiet-fd-parity
archetypes.rationale: The new diagnostic() in logging_util.py writes to fd 4 without the _self_initialized_quiet guard that BreadcrumbWriter.emit uses; plan_block_strip_body_main calls quiet_init only on the malformed path; and _validate_positive_issue's isdecimal() check may admit leading-zero issue values.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine python/logging_util.py diagnostic(): unlike BreadcrumbWriter.emit, it writes to fd 4 whenever _quiet_active() returns true without first checking _self_initialized_quiet — determine whether LARCH_QUIET_ACTIVE set externally (without calling quiet_init) can cause writes to a caller's unexpected fd 4, and compare against the guard pattern in BreadcrumbWriter.emit. Examine python/issue_wire.py plan_block_strip_body_main: quiet_init is called only on the malformed path, not before any emit_kv call; verify the MALFORMED= KV reliably reaches stdout under an active quiet parent and that the success path does not lose output. Examine _validate_positive_issue: isdecimal() combined with '== 0' accepts '00', '01', '001', etc. as positive integers — check whether the bash originals rejected leading-zero values and whether this constitutes a parity gap. Also check strip_named_block's error return: it returns ('', malformed) not (None, malformed) and confirm all callers handle the empty-string sentinel correctly. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: resource-double-parse
archetypes.rationale: issue_edit_body_with_retry creates a NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) and relies solely on a finally block for cleanup, risking leaks on SIGKILL; the replace path in named_block_write redundantly calls strip_named_block then discards the result and re-classifies, creating confusion about which copy of the body is canonical.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine python/gh.py issue_edit_body_with_retry: the temp file is created with delete=False and cleaned up only in a finally block — assess the temp-file leak risk on process kill and whether the file permissions (default umask) expose redacted issue body content to other processes. In python/issue_wire.py named_block_write's replace branch (markers_present=True, delete=False), strip_named_block is called and the stripped result stored in _stripped but never used; then _classify_named_block_lines is called again on current_body — verify this double-classification always produces the same span as the first parse and assess whether an inline strip-and-insert using _stripped would be safer. Examine plan_scope_paths_main: int(exc.code or 0) is called on SystemExit.code which argparse may set to a non-numeric string on usage errors — determine the actual failure mode and whether the caller exits with the right code. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
